about.tool: A fine, flexible pointed steel pen.
about.slant: 52 degrees from the horizontal for the main strokes; 30 degrees for the connecting curves.
about.proportions: 1 : 2 : 3 in spaces (the height of small i): short letters 1 space, t d p 2, loops and capitals 3; lower loops 2 below.
about.features: Built from seven principles: straight line, right curve, left curve, extended loop, direct oval, reversed oval and capital stem. Small letters are light and semi-angular: short turns at the top, angular joins at the base, long connecting curves. Capitals are built on ovals and the capital stem with its base oval. Simplified here: the standard capitals without flourishes, M, H, K, T and F a few per cent narrower to fit, and every downstroke swells slightly (the pen rule), where Spencerian shades only a few strokes and each capital once.
about.history: Platt Rogers Spencer's American hand, taught from the 1850s in the Spencerian copybooks and business colleges, and the standard American business and correspondence hand until the Palmer method replaced it around 1900.
